Principle: Count REF edges from RESET until first FB edge; count=ceil(D/T). count=1 -> D<T (rail); count=2 -> 1T basin; count>=3 -> harmonic. Steer delay until count=2.
New_Hardware: 2-3 bit counter, decode logic, mode FSM, coarse delay control (switched caps or DAC)
Area_Power_Qualitative: Small digital; modest analog coarse control
Startup_Sequence: RESET -> hold CP off -> count k -> if k!=2 steer VCDL -> repeat -> k==2 -> enable CP
Fine_Lock_Handoff: Gate CP off during count; release when k==2 stable for N cycles; FSM hysteresis prevents chatter
Failure_Modes: In-flight delay change corrupts count (mitigate: CP off); exact k=1/k=2 boundary ambiguous; glitches; frequency change mid-count
Suitability_25_200MHz: Good if counter resolves 5ns at 200MHz (feasible in Sky130)
Evidence_Level: Level B behavioral concept; NOT simulated as a circuit

Principle: Split VCDL into digitally-switched coarse section plus analog fine section. Coarse sets approximate delay; fine PFD/CP removes residual.
New_Hardware: Coarse switched loads/caps, coarse control DAC, MUX, extra buffering
Area_Power_Qualitative: Moderate-to-high; roughly increased VCDL complexity and routing
Startup_Sequence: Select coarse code (from band or count) -> allow fine loop to lock
Fine_Lock_Handoff: Standard PFD/CP takes over fine residual after coarse settles
Failure_Modes: Coarse step too large -> overshoot basin; coarse/fine mismatch; extra load on taps; still needs a period estimate to choose code
Suitability_25_200MHz: Good if coarse range covers 1T across PVT
Distinguishes_1T_vs_Harmonic: NO by itself - needs edge count or HLD
Evidence_Level: Level B concept; band ranges from dll_model.py

Principle: Use existing RANGE[1:0] to select one of three delay ranges. Narrows D/T uncertainty but does not set it.
Startup_Sequence: Choose band from RANGE -> existing startup (min delay)
Failure_Modes: Band alone cannot place D in basin; min-delay startup still rails at all frequencies; max-delay only works at 25/30MHz
Suitability_25_200MHz: Band ranges verified 25-200MHz but basin placement NOT guaranteed
Evidence_Level: Level B - computed from BANDS in dll_model.py

Principle: Use UP/DOWN and PFD reset state to detect startup condition. Counting REF edges while UP asserted is equivalent to Option A. UP pulse width alone is ambiguous.
New_Hardware: Small digital FSM tapping existing PFD signals
Startup_Sequence: RESET -> monitor PFD -> count REF while UP asserted -> steer -> enable fine
Fine_Lock_Handoff: CP gated during coarse; release on k==2
Failure_Modes: UP width identical for 0.68T and 1.68T (verified); needs actual edge count not pulse width; PFD dead zone; metastability
Suitability_25_200MHz: Good at 25-200MHz if FSM fast enough
Distinguishes_1T_vs_Harmonic: YES if it counts edges; NO if it uses pulse width only
Evidence_Level: Level B - pulse-width ambiguity verified in diag_pulse_width; ignore-count verified in diag_ignore_count

Principle: E1 multiphase harmonic lock detector; E2 replica VCDL as VCO (PLL-assisted coarse); E3 stopwatch/N-detector measuring D/T; E4 binary search on phase error
New_Hardware: Multiphase comparators; OR second VCDL+PLL; OR replica delay model+counter; OR SAR controller
Area_Power_Qualitative: Varies: E2 ~2x area/power; E1/E3 moderate; E4 moderate
Startup_Sequence: Depends on sub-option; all require extra acquisition phase
Fine_Lock_Handoff: Varies; all then hand off to fine loop
Failure_Modes: E2 area/power doubling; E3 process/temp tracking between model and real line; E4 needs polarity signal that PFD one-sided transfer does not provide; glitches
Suitability_25_200MHz: E1 wide range demonstrated in 0.13um 25-500MHz; others plausible
Distinguishes_1T_vs_Harmonic: E1 and E3 YES; E2 indirectly; E4 unclear with this PFD
Evidence_Level: Level B concept only; literature cited
References: IET HLD 2015; Razavi 2018; Baker thesis; arxiv 2501.13238
